$comment: Hand-edited (docs/SCHEMA.md). The North Bay horsecars: Santa Rosa's 1877 line and the Petaluma Street Railroad. Research: docs/research/phase-2c.md.

lines.name: Santa Rosa horsecars, Fourth St and McDonald Ave
lines.summary: Santa Rosa's first street railway: horsecars from the San Francisco & North Pacific depot east along Fourth St, past the courthouse, to McDonald Ave, then north to the cemetery, 1.62 miles.
lines.fate_note: Never electrified: the Petaluma & Santa Rosa, which took the horsecar lines over, laid its own track on Fourth St in 1905 and never used their franchises (CRC Decision No. 2348). When the horses stopped isn't known.

route.note: Operation was suspended early in 1893, during the lawsuit over its franchise (Borden).
Resumed in 1898, after the Union Street Railway bought the line (Borden).

running.note: The Santa Rosa Street Rwy. Co., with the Central and Union lines, reported for the year 1902.
1.5 miles of horse track, 7 horses and 5 cars.
Controlled and operated by the Santa Rosa Street Railways, with 7 horses for its 7 miles.

sources.note: "during the year 1877 completed the portion in controversy in this action, and has ever since continued to operate that portion", on Fourth St; operated continuously from 1877 to 1891.

"opened for service one year later" than its June 5, 1877 charter; "Its 1.62 miles of track ran east along Fourth Street from the San Francisco & North Pacific Railroad depot to McDonald Ave., then north along this street to the cemetery"; four horse cars on 3 ft 6 in gauge. "Early in 1893, operation was suspended owing to litigation about charter rights"; bought by the Union's directors on December 27, 1897 (p. 3; December 24 on p. 4), and "operation was resumed the following year"; under the Santa Rosa Street Railways from 1902 (p. 4). The horsecars ran "until 1905" (p. 5), but "How long these horse cars continued to operate after they were acquired is not known" (p. 6).
February 1897: "This company is now in litigation and has suspended operations."
Bought by the Union Street Railway on the afternoon of December 24, 1897.
The Petaluma & Santa Rosa bought "the two original horse-car lines formerly operating in Petaluma and Santa Rosa" but never operated under their franchises.

lines.notes: Opens in 1877, the year the Supreme Court found the Fourth St track completed and running; Borden has 1878. Its owner sold it on December 24, 1897 (the Los Angeles Times's dispatch of that day, and Borden on p. 4; his p. 3 has December 27). Its end isn't sourced: Borden gives 1905 in one place and says in another that how long the horsecars ran "is not known"; directories list it, with horses, to March 1906, and the Railroad Commission calls the lines "formerly operating" in 1915. Not drawn: the South Side (Union) line to the race track (1888) and the Central's Humboldt St line (1892), whose streets of the day aren't placed.

lines.name: Petaluma Street Railroad, F St to the fairgrounds
lines.summary: Horsecars from the car barn at 12th and F Sts by F St, 6th St, Liberty St, Western Ave and Kentucky St to Washington St, then across Petaluma Creek and the railroad to the fairgrounds.
lines.fate_note: Bought by the Petaluma & Santa Rosa in 1903 for its franchise rights, which that company never used (CRC Decision No. 2348); when the horses stopped isn't known.

running.note: The Petaluma Street Rwy. Co. reported for December 1, 1901 to November 30, 1902, with 1.81 miles of track.
2 miles of horse track, 4 cars and 4 horses.

sources.note: Incorporated October 14, 1889; "an 1897 map shows the following route: from 12th St. via F St., 6th St., Liberty St., Western Ave., Kentucky St., Washington St., across Petaluma Creek and across the San Francisco & North Pacific Railroad tracks to just beyond Mary St.", with a branch into the fairgrounds; sold under foreclosure in 1900, and to the Petaluma & Santa Rosa in 1903.
Sold at sheriff's sale to the Wickersham Banking Company on September 27, 1897.
"The properties of this company were sold at foreclosure sale in 1900 to the Wickersham Banking Co., The road is now owned and managed by Thomas Maclay."
"Purchase of Petaluma horse-car line for its rights, $2,790.00".

lines.notes: Drawn for the years a source shows it running (decision 20), on the streets of Borden's 1897 map. Its opening isn't sourced; it was incorporated on October 14, 1889 (Borden). Sold at sheriff's sale on September 27, 1897 (Los Angeles Times); Borden and the 1903 directory have a foreclosure sale in 1900. The 1905 directory still lists its horses, as sold to the Petaluma & Santa Rosa. Not drawn: the stretch from Payran St to just beyond Mary St, and the fairgrounds branch, for want of the old Mary St's place.
